source: J.-L. Orgiazzi, C. Deng, D. Layden, R. Marchildon, F. Kitapli, F. Shen, M. Bal, F. R. Ong, A. Lupascu, 'Flux qubits in a planar circuit quantum electrodynamics architecture: quantum control and decoherence', Phys. Rev. B 93, 104518 (2016); arXiv:1407.1346
location: arXiv:1407.1346v1 full text (the only arXiv version; the PRB version of record was not accessible beyond its abstract, which rounds the relaxation times to '5 and 10 us' and quotes the qubit-qubit coupling as 38 MHz). Running text of the relaxation and dephasing sections around Figs. 2-3, and the Supplementary Material (setup). Per-quantity locations below.
comment: The Lupascu group's time-domain (Ramsey / spin-echo) decoherence measurements on persistent-current flux qubits, included because the harvesting-device paper (janzen_2023_fig6) gives pure dephasing only as a plot-digitized transmission-fit quantity. This is a DIFFERENT device: two four-junction aluminium flux qubits coupled to a coplanar-waveguide RESONATOR (cQED readout), not the tunable-coupler qubit on an open waveguide. Its numbers are measured floors for what Lupascu-group flux qubits reach, not parameters of the harvesting device. Rate convention: the paper prints the pure-dephasing rates as exponential decay rates in us^-1 (fit C(tau) = exp(-Gamma_1 tau/2) exp(-Gamma_phi tau) ...). The loader's unit table has no inverse-microsecond unit and its 'MHz' entry applies the energy rule (x 2pi), which would be WRONG for these rates; they are therefore stored in s^-1 under the 'rad/s' entry (a decay rate in s^-1 is an angular rate: no 2pi), with the printed string kept in 'printed'. That is a prefix rescaling (x 1e6), not a convention change.
provenance_tags: Per-quantity 'provenance' is 'transcribed' throughout; no synthetic or derived quantities ('synthetic_quantities' empty, asserted by tests/test_experiments_io.py). 'kind' is 'measured' unless stated ('bound', 'calculated').

T1_qubit1.note: 'The energy relaxation times are T_1 = 5.3 us and 9.6 us for qubits 1 and 2 respectively at their symmetry points' (PRB abstract rounds to '5 and 10 us')

intrinsic_T1_qubit1.note: 'If the relaxation due to these sources (Purcell effect through the first 10 resonator modes and the control line) is excluded, we calculate intrinsic relaxation times of 7 (20) us for qubit 1 (2)'

pure_dephasing_rate_ramsey_qubit1.note: 'At the symmetry point, decay is exponential, with rates Gamma_phi,R = 0.77 (0.90) us^-1 for Ramsey and Gamma_phi,E = 1.03 (1.85) us^-1 for spin-echo measurements for qubit 1 (2)'. Stored as 0.77e6 s^-1 (see file comment on the unit); the printed echo rates exceeding the Ramsey rates is as published

dephasing_character_symmetry_point.value: exponential decay at the symmetry point, dominated by a nearly frequency-independent white noise source (dynamical-decoupling noise spectroscopy, Fig. 3(f)); Gaussian (1/f flux-noise) decay away from it

flux_noise_amplitude_qubit1.note: 1/f flux noise PSD A/|omega|, from the slope of the spin-echo dephasing rate versus flux bias; 'slightly larger than for the smaller aluminum flux qubits' of earlier work, 'in qualitative agreement with size scaling'

readout_contrast.note: 'Dispersive qubit state readout reaches a maximum contrast of 72%'; 'limited primarily by the initialization procedure which is based on thermalization'

mixing_chamber_temperature.note: 'The temperature measured at the mixing chamber level of the custom designed top loading probe, to which the device copper box is attached, was 40 mK'

resonator_decay_rate_mode1.note: kappa = 882 kHz, 'the resonator decay rate for the first mode'; printed as kHz, so the loader's x 2pi energy rule inherits the same factor-2pi ambiguity as the parent device paper

thermal_photon_number_bound.note: 'an upper bound for the thermal photon number n_th < 0.02' in the readout resonator, from spectroscopy and simulation

photon_shot_noise_dephasing_bound.note: 'the dephasing rate, given by kappa n_th ... is smaller than 18 kHz, thus a negligible contribution' at the symmetry point

qubit_qubit_coupling.location: coupling paragraph (Fig. 4); PRB abstract quotes '38 MHz'
qubit_qubit_coupling.note: resonator-mediated qubit-qubit coupling 'of 37.8 MHz', characterised spectroscopically

quasiparticle_density_estimate.value: 0.12 um^-3 (qubit 1), 0.04 um^-3 (qubit 2), non-equilibrium quasiparticle density that would account for the intrinsic T_1
